about.title: Stanton Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Stanton sits at a crossroads of some of Orange County's busier surface streets, and that traffic shows up in the numbers: 111 injury collisions and 139 people hurt in the most recent reporting year, with Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. a common time for crashes to occur. Corridors like Beach Boulevard, Katella Avenue, Cerritos Avenue, and Route 39 see steady volume, and a collision on any of them can leave you dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who calls before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured Stanton residents with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Getting matched with someone who understands local roads and California claims procedure costs you nothing to start.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Deadline Is Closer Than It Seems
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or public bus — was involved. Waiting to sort out evidence can quietly cost you your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You Fast
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation gets reduced by whatever percentage of blame you're assigned — even 10% matters. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer is often used to inflate that percentage before you've had a chance to review the facts.

items.title: No Cap Means Full Value Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, so how your claim is documented and presented can materially affect what you're offered. An attorney working on contingency has an incentive to build that case carefully, not settle it quickly.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to find inconsistencies or get you to downplay your injuries, which can reduce what you're eventually offered. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash near Beach Boulevard or Katella Avenue — does it matter where it happened?
items.answer: The location itself doesn't determine your legal rights, but details like the intersection, traffic signals, and any city or Caltrans involvement can matter for evidence gathering and, in some cases, shorter filing deadlines against public entities. That's part of why documenting the scene early is useful.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward after you're matched.
